doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

title: Substitute teaching in Las Vegas with his degree
summary: During the Dunes years Hal substitute-taught by day, using his college degree.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well for a guy who couldn’t find a real job I think you’ve done well for yourself.

You know, thank you — and you know I never planned anything other than to get a degree in college, and the only time I used it was when I was in Vegas when I was working at the Dunes at Viva La Girls show. Our first show was 11:00 at night and then 1:00 in the morning and 3:00 in the morning. It was an hour and twenty minute show and 40 minutes off. And then that was the whole routine. The rest of the day until 11:00 at night was mine. So then I decided I’m going to do some teaching — substitute teaching — because I had my degree and I could do something useful during the afternoon. So I’d get to bed around 5:00 in the morning. I’d get a call at 6 to teach at North High School, and I thought well I’ll do this a few times just to say I used my degree. I ended up getting called every day for that whole year, during the school days. And I went from being a Spanish teacher to an English teacher to a band teacher one time out of that whole year. But, and then the kid saw me up there and they’d start playing around on the horns, you know when I told them to stop. And then when we were playing somebody was screwing around, they didn’t think I knew. I’d stop and say, “You want to stand up — you want to play a solo? Then I want to hear it. Stand up and play.” Nobody would stand up because they didn’t know who I was talking to. So I’d say, “You.” Get all embarrassed and said, “I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I didn’t mean that.” So anyway I got to use my degree one time.
